reason: This biblical passage (Exodus 5-10) does not depict Yahweh complaining about the people. The text focuses on God's commands to Moses, the hardening of Pharaoh's heart, and the successive plagues. The complaints present in the text come from other parties: Moses complains to Yahweh about the worsening situation of the people ('Adonai, why have you brought trouble upon this people?'), the Israelite foremen complain to Pharaoh about harsh treatment, and Pharaoh complains about the destruction caused by the plagues. Yahweh's speech centers on declarations of power and instructions for the plagues, not expressions of dissatisfaction with the Hebrew people.
